# Cost and sustainability — 1.1.0

## Apply when

Use when options materially differ in build cost, operating cost, licensing, consumption, staffing, or resource efficiency.

## Required context

Budget boundary, demand model, regions, environments, retention, availability target, staffing assumptions, licensing, growth horizon, and cost owner.

## Clarify

Ask which costs are in scope, which currency and pricing date apply, what utilization is expected, how shared costs are allocated, and which cost threshold changes the decision.

## Deterministic checks

- Flag estimates without quantities, units, time horizon, pricing date, currency, or uncertainty range.
- Identify dominant cost drivers, idle capacity, data transfer, storage growth, licensing, support, and operational labor.
- Compare unit economics at normal, peak, and plausible growth scenarios.
- Check cost allocation, budget alerts, anomaly detection, commitments, and exit costs.
- Do not make environmental claims without a defined metric and authoritative evidence.

## Research

Treat every price, discount, SKU, and regional availability statement as time-sensitive. Use official pricing and licensing sources and record retrieval date; state that negotiated pricing may differ.

## Output

Produce assumption-based cost ranges, unit-cost drivers, sensitivity analysis, optimization tradeoffs, and standard findings.
